items.text: Messages from students and families across Iran indicate increased security and ideological control in schools. Students say school officials force them to participate in government and military programs or ideological ceremonies.

Marta Shahbazi, an Iranian-origin researcher and Cambridge University professor, died in a deadly train collision in Spain. The accident, caused by human error, resulted in 69 deaths. Shahbazi worked in developmental biology and had expressed support for the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' protests.

The spokesperson of the Islamic Republic's Ministry of Foreign Affairs claimed that because the US and Israel have assassinated "Ali Khamenei" as the holder of the fatwa banning the use of nuclear weapons, the Islamic Republic is considering changing its nuclear doctrine. Esmail Baqaei emphasized that the issue of changing Iran's nuclear doctrine is a real matter and should not be limited only to domestic discussions.

The coordination manager of the National Gas Company announced the issuance of heavy bills, gas cutoffs for high-consumption subscribers, and increased fines as the cold season approaches and the industrial energy crisis intensifies. This news was evaluated by Ata Hosseinian, an economic and energy journalist.

French media have examined the potential consequences of the US midterm elections for Washington's relations with Europe and Donald Trump's policies regarding the Ukraine war and Middle East developments.

Tucker Carlson, an American journalist, claimed that the Trump administration under pressure from Netanyahu might launch a nuclear attack on Iran within a few days. He identified the likely target as the Koh-e-Kalang facility in central Iran and warned that such an action could endanger the lives of 100 million people and push the world toward a third world war. Maria Zakharova, spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry, also expressed concern about plans for a new military action against Iran.

Citizens in Hamedan and Tehran complain about high medical and drug costs. Supplemental insurance does not cover some expenses, and patients give up treatment due to financial inability. Drug prices range from hundreds of thousands to millions of tomans.

Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the necessity of public participation in governing the country during a meeting with governors and mayors of major cities, stating that the country can emerge strongly from enemy threats. He added that if the people support the officials, no harm can be done, and called for the use of local capacities and coordination in provinces. He also stressed preventing the closure of production units and providing cheaper services to deprived areas.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the large presence of American weapons and warships in the region is not just a show of force. He added that the US wants to bring Iran to the negotiating table through military threats and may carry out a limited high-intensity attack if Iran refuses. Bakhshayesh described the current situation as "neither war nor peace," which has become a tangled confusion.

Ilam telecommunications retirees gathered today, Tuesday, 11 Aban, to protest the uncertainty of overdue claims and livelihood problems. They protested the non-implementation of the welfare agreement since 1400, regulation 89/24, supplementary insurance issues, and the increase in retirees' payment shares. They also demanded accountability from the Executive Headquarters of Imam's Order and the Basij Cooperative Foundation regarding their rights and claims.

A video shows the mother of the late Mohammad Amin Kholaseh-Shar mourning at the graves of him and his brother Arsalan. Mohammad Amin, 23 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Fardis, and his brother Arsalan ended his life about a month later due to grief over losing him.

On Tuesday, 11 Aban, a report was made about the livelihood crisis and inability to pay expenses. It was stated that the government does not return the millions and billions of shopkeepers' money related to ration cards. Also, living costs such as a simple birthday for a child, children's clothes, and train tickets have increased sharply.

Hassan Hassanzadeh, commander of Tehran's IRGC, said the first Janfada brigade of Iran has been organized, completed its advanced training, and is preparing for practical courses and specialized shooting range exercises. He added that soon the organization of Janfada brigades and battalions will take shape, and convoys of Janfada fighters will be dispatched to operational areas in the south and west of the country.

Aref Nasiri, a resident of Abdanan, was summoned to the Ilam Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office following a search of his home and the seizure of Starlink satellite internet equipment by security forces. The security forces entered his home in his absence and confiscated the Starlink device on the early morning of 29 Mehr.

Reports indicate a significant increase in the supply and sale of gold and silver plaques with symbols related to the Pahlavi era, including the Lion and Sun flag and the Pahlavi crown. Simultaneously, the Police Department in Mashhad banned the sale of gold with Lion and Sun and Pahlavi symbols. This issue was evaluated by Forough Kanani, a sociology researcher.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said the Iranian government knows that if it loses its nuclear leverage and the Strait of Hormuz, it will no longer have the power to confront the US. He added that the government's insistence on maintaining these levers may push Trump toward a decision to end the Islamic Republic, a decision that could happen at any moment. However, Trump, due to considerations related to power transition and keeping diplomatic channels open, has left ways open for negotiation with Tehran.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Canada gathered in Toronto on Sunday, 10 Aban, and chanted "Long live the Shah, long live Iran."

Two women arrested during the December 1404 protests were each sentenced to 22 years in prison by Branch 23 of Tehran's Revolutionary Court. These two women are in Qarchak Varamin prison and share the case with three other defendants, including Mahdi Jalali and two others sentenced to death. Initially, these two women faced the death penalty, but the judge reduced their sentence to 22 years in prison.

The Public Relations of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army announced that an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz area had an accident and caught fire due to hitting a naval mine. The oil tanker had turned off its navigation systems. The Navy warned that uncoordinated movement in dangerous areas can lead to hitting naval mines and fires.

The commander of Rezvanshahr police announced the arrest of a 37-year-old citizen in the Peresar district of this county on charges of causing public unrest and propaganda against the regime in cyberspace. Mohammad Mirbaghian stated that this citizen was identified and arrested by the public security police and was referred to the judicial authority after the case was filed.

Ahmad Reza Radan repeated Mojtaba Khamenei's recent threat, saying that if war restarts, the Islamic Republic's armed forces will target any point in the world. Radan threatened that all countries supporting the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic in any way will be targeted for attack.

Reuters reported that Wang Yi, China's foreign minister, warned during a meeting with Musaed Al Aiban, Saudi Arabia's national security advisor, in Beijing that the Gulf region is at a "sensitive juncture between war and peace." Wang Yi expressed hope that all parties can end conflicts through negotiation and emphasized the need to protect energy security and shipping routes in the region. Additionally, Mohammed bin Salman sent a message to Xi Jinping regarding bilateral relations and ways to develop cooperation.

The school principal said that on 13 Aban, students must attend a rally and anyone who does not will have their discipline score reduced. At Payame Noor University in Urmia, the tuition is at least 12 million tomans but there are insufficient facilities. The Minister of Science emphasized that universities must be in-person even under the likely occurrence of war.

Today, a group of greenhouse farmers from Mirjaveh, Khash, and Saravan counties gathered in front of the Sistan and Baluchestan governor's office in Zahedan, demanding the allocation of fuel quotas for greenhouses. The protest started on Saturday, 9 Aban, and the protesters have been present daily. The farmers said their visits to the Oil Company and the Agricultural Jihad Organization have been fruitless, and the necessary fuel for heating greenhouses has not been allocated.
Benjamin Kouhkan, one of the detainees of the 1401 protests who is serving his sentence in Zahedan prison, was sent on leave yesterday.

A Learjet 60 aircraft crashed in a residential area in Elm Beach, Florida, on Sunday, October 31. According to US transportation officials, all nine occupants died. In recorded air traffic control conversations, the pilot reported a rapid loss of altitude, declared an emergency, and said, "We are going to hit the ground" and "We are out of time."

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, stated that Iran is more prepared than before for both diplomacy and military action and warned that if the US takes military action again, it will face worse consequences. He said that indirect talks between Tehran and Washington have intensified and Qatar and Pakistan play an active mediator role. Araghchi added that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz depends on Iran's conditions being accepted, and if accepted, negotiations will resume.

Shahed Alavi, a member of Iran International's editorial board, said regarding Amnesty International's campaign to identify those responsible for the killing of Iranians that the world is sufficiently aware of the Islamic Republic's crimes, but what matters is turning this awareness into practical action. He added that the goal of this campaign is to identify the perpetrators of repression, provide the basis for their accountability in international courts, and prevent the recurrence of killings. According to him, the system of repression in the Islamic Republic is not limited to security agencies, and the foreign policy apparatus and the judiciary also play a role in this repression.

The Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic announced that Mohsen Rezaei and Vladimir Putin held a phone conversation about regional and global developments, especially the situation in West Asia. The two sides emphasized continuing strategic cooperation between the Islamic Republic and Russia within the framework of the roadmap set by the leaders of the two countries.

Raha Bahraini, a human rights lawyer and Amnesty International researcher on Iran, said Amnesty International, in solidarity with families seeking justice, is trying to establish a mechanism for international criminal justice so that those responsible for the killing and repression of Iranians are held accountable.

The statements of the Minister of Energy regarding Mojtaba Khamenei's recommendation to produce electricity at homes and sell or transfer surplus electricity to neighbors received humorous and critical reactions from Iran International's audience. Citizens say the region's leading power cannot even supply electricity to the homes of its own people.

Sohrab Bakhtiari-Zadeh, head coach of Esteghlal, said in a press conference before the match against Al Shamal Qatar that tomorrow's game will be tough for both teams and they must try with all their might. He said about Esteghlal's previous wins against Qatari teams that Qatari teams are always strong and they must play with minimal mistakes. Bakhtiari-Zadeh added that his team has the quality and focus needed for tomorrow's game and hopes to earn the three points.

It has been reported that Donald Trump, after a phone call with Netanyahu about an attack on Iran, said he would soon deliver a heavy blow. This comes as the Islamic Republic is reportedly concerned about collapse due to armed forces entering from the borders or people returning to the streets.

The Deputy Minister of Health announced that about 50% of the country's hospitals face safety challenges due to their age and structural problems, and some centers have become fire hazards for patients and staff. Renovation and replacement of about 500 hospitals, which required over 500 hundred billion tomans two years ago, now need 800 to 900 hundred billion tomans due to increased costs. Also, the capacity of burn beds in the country is about half of the required standard, and some provinces lack specialized burn centers and sufficient intensive care beds.

Tractor is hosting Neftchi Fargona from Uzbekistan today in Oman, at the start of the fourth week of the AFC Champions League Elite. The AFC has reportedly withdrawn hosting rights from Iranian teams after January 2026.

Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy for International Affairs of the Supreme National Security Council Secretariat, emphasized the creation of a new security structure in the region without US interference and Israeli influence during a meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Monday, November 2, 2026. He stated that the Islamic Republic seeks to restore stability to the region through new security arrangements in which the US would not interfere and Israel would not be able to exert influence. Bagheri Kani also welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping's initiative in this regard.

Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the importance of overcoming the challenges and crises created by enemies for Iran and said, "We try to solve the problem through dialogue." The head of the government in Iran also stressed that Mojtaba Khamenei, the leader of the Islamic Republic, has given the government powers to advance the dialogues, but did not provide further details about these powers.

Navid Mohammadzadeh said he does not want to publicly screen his film in Iran due to censorship and prefers to consider it a personal work. He intended to depict the reality of young people's lives and Generation Z, adding that Iranian women have effectively gained the right to choose their clothing in the past four years. Mohammadzadeh is participating in the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival with his directorial debut film "I'm Really Not a Special Person."

Yaser Asani, Esteghlal star, said in a press conference before the match against Al Shamal Qatar that Esteghlal is the biggest name in Asia and has many fans wherever it plays. He added that the three points in tomorrow's match are very important and Esteghlal has great players. Asani said about hosting in Basra that he hopes Esteghlal fans and Iranians in Iraq will come to the stadium to support the team.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said he does not want the war with Iran to become a long-term conflict like the Vietnam War. He added that the US is in the seventh month of the war and 18 American military personnel have been killed so far. Trump also said that American forces have carried out heavy attacks several times but have not had direct clashes in recent months.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of Iranians residing in the UK gathered in Leeds on Sunday, 10 Aban to commemorate Cyrus the Great Day and the birthday of Prince Reza Pahlavi, singing the anthem "Ey Iran" together.

Sajjad Razavi, Deputy Minister of Health, announced that the number of burn beds in Iran is about half the required standard and that specialized burn intensive care beds are also insufficient. He warned that about 50% of hospitals in Iran face safety challenges due to aging and structural problems. Razavi said some provinces lack specialized burn centers and hospital safety requires fundamental measures.

The owner of Ahold Delhaize chain supermarkets announced that an IT incident last night affected refrigerators and freezers in dozens of stores in Belgium and Luxembourg. Two Swedish chain stores, ICA and Coop, also reported a similar temperature increase, and one of the stores attributed it to a cyberattack. A Delhaize spokesperson said the temperature of the cooling systems rose and the company is investigating.

The executive secretary of the Saveh Workers' House stated that workers of the Benro automotive company in Saveh have not yet received their salaries for Mehr month. He also criticized the intermittent interruption of these workers' health insurance and their lack of benefits paid by the central Saipa company.

Yossi Cohen, former head of Mossad, predicted that another targeted military attack against the Islamic Republic will occur. He said the Islamic Republic is still developing its facilities and may rebuild some damaged centers. Cohen also said that the military cooperation between Israel and the US to target Iran's nuclear facilities and ballistic missiles has been one of his long-standing goals.

A citizen was beaten by a border guard officer at the Milak terminal in Sistan and Baluchestan province. The offending officer has been arrested, and the direct commander of this officer is also under judicial prosecution.

The Kepler Institute estimated Iran's floating crude oil volume outside the maritime blockade at nearly 89 million barrels in early summer. These reserves decreased to about 15 million barrels at the start of autumn, and now, according to Kepler's latest assessment, Iran's crude oil inventory in this area has reached zero. Interview with Homayoun Falakshahi, oil and energy expert at the Kepler Institute.

Farzin Nadimi said a US nuclear attack on the underground facilities of Kolanggezla may cause destruction but also carries the risk of radioactive material release and widespread environmental contamination. He added the attack might extend to missile bases, military industries, and command centers of the Islamic Republic. Nadimi also said Tehran's military response could expand the conflict to the energy infrastructure of regional countries and increase the likelihood of a prolonged war.

Meir Javedanfar, an analyst on Israeli affairs, said about the competition to form a government in the country that given Netanyahu's history of refusing to coalition with opposition parties, it is possible that Gadi Eizenkot can gain the support of Arab parties. Conversely, if Netanyahu can bring at least one major opposition party with him, he will be very close to forming a government.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Norway held a ceremony for Cyrus the Great Day and the birthday of Prince Reza Pahlavi in Oslo on Sunday, 10 Aban.

Hamzeh Darvish, a Sunni prisoner, has been held in solitary confinement for about 38 days after being transferred to Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. During this time, he has only been able to make phone calls to his family three times. Prison officials stated that his solitary confinement is by order of the case judge.

The Telegram channel Daneshjooyan Mottahed reported that the student councils of eight universities in Tehran jointly wrote a letter to Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, protesting the security forces' treatment of students regarding dress code, movement restrictions, and pressure on union activities, demanding a halt to these actions. In the letter, the student councils warned that increased interference in students' daily lives in recent months, including arbitrary actions about dress code, dormitory restrictions, and turning universities into arenas for political purges, has affected the dignity and peace of the academic community. The signatories also demanded an end to pressure and filing cases against union activists, guaranteeing the independence of student councils, and reviewing unfair disciplinary regulations, procedures, and rulings.
It was reported that the Iran war is among the five important issues for Americans 24 hours before the elections.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the imminent risk of execution for Abolfazl Ebrahimi and Amirhossein Maleki, two 20-year-old youths arrested during the December uprising. Their families have been called for a final visit to Dastgerd prison in Isfahan, and the execution order may be carried out within the next hours. The office described the trial process as a show trial and urged people not to remain silent to prevent their execution.

The approval of the "Law on Organizing and Supervising Border Trade" in 1402 is recognized as an official acknowledgment of the issues of kolbari and the importance of the economic conditions in border areas. Despite this law, reports of deaths among kolbars and fuel carriers at Iran's borders continue. UN experts on September 23, 2026, highlighted these tensions and emphasized that economic, social, and political factors are at the root of these problems.
It was reported that Netanyahu pressures Trump to resume attacks on Iran.

Tractor football team drew 2-2 with Neftchi Uzbekistan in the fourth week of the Asian Champions League. Tractor's goals were scored by Tomislav Stirkali in the 82nd minute and Masoud Zaerkazemini in the 90+9th minute. Tractor played with 10 men from the 61st minute after Farshad Faraji was sent off and now stands 13th in the West group of the Asian Champions League with 2 points from 4 games.

Danny Danon, Israel's representative to the United Nations, stated that Israel and the US have the technology to know what is happening inside Iran. He said Tehran has not stopped its efforts to acquire nuclear weapons. Danon also emphasized that no one in Israel or the US is talking about using nuclear weapons against Iran.

The mother of Matin Parvizi, 22, who was shot dead with a military bullet in Zanjan on 18 Dey 1404, said in a video from her son's grave that she will find his killer one day, even if she is not alive, others will find him.

At least seven protest gatherings were held. The strike of private sector unit line drivers in Yazd reached its third day. Retired telecommunications workers in Tehran, Isfahan, Sanandaj, Bijar, Kermanshah, and Ilam gathered in protest against the non-implementation of regulation 89/24, the status of supplementary insurance, and their overdue demands.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in an interview with Israel's Channel 12 that he is in no hurry to resume war with Iran and is currently continuing economic pressure on the Islamic Republic. He said that contrary to his expectations, the leaders of the Islamic Republic do not feel urgency to reach an agreement but now more than ever want a deal with the US. Trump also said about the Tehran-Washington talks mediated by Qatar that the negotiations are progressing well but they are not sure who the decision-maker is.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that targeting officials of the Islamic Republic does not necessarily lead to regime change, and attacking the country's infrastructure can also cause irreparable damage. He added that the success of a short and extensive attack to eliminate the military capability of the Islamic Republic is not certain, and without an effective plan, there is a risk of the conflict expanding into a protracted war with heavy consequences for Iran and the region.

A report states that two Afghan prisoners sentenced to death for drug-related crimes were executed at Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan on the early morning of 29 Mehr. Additionally, a child offender prisoner previously sentenced to death for murder at age 17 was executed in Dezful Prison on 28 Mordad.

Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher living in Nurabad Mamasani and imprisoned in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz, was physically assaulted by a prison official on Sunday, 10 Aban 1405. A knowledgeable source said that while he was following up on his eye treatment and despite having permission to see a doctor, he was assaulted for unknown reasons and suffered injuries to his head, face, nose, and back.

Alireza Faghani, an international football referee, expressed condolences on the death of Hamid Alidousti in a video on his Instagram page and said that he was too much for Iranian football. Faghani also said that unfortunately, there are decision-makers in Iranian football whose football knowledge and literacy are one hundredth of these dear ones.

The UK prosecution stated in its final summary that three defendants knowingly assisted the IRGC in planning an attack on two Iran International journalists by visiting the targets' addresses and taking photos and videos. William Emlyn Jones, the prosecution lawyer, said at the start of the fifth week of the trial in London that the defendants' activities matched what the IRGC requested. He added that the attack not occurring does not negate the defendants' assistance to the IRGC.

On Thursday, 7 Aban, the family home of Pouya Taher and Rojan Ahyayi, a couple residing in Mahabad, as well as their business premises, were searched by security forces. The security forces searched the home in the absence of Pouya Taher and his wife and insulted his elderly parents during the action. This report was published by Harana News Agency.
Two men in Tehran, who are cousins, were arrested on charges of sexual assault against a young girl. Judicial investigations regarding this case are ongoing.
Javad Khaki, a political prisoner, was granted a three-day leave from the Central Prison of Karaj on Sunday, 10 Aban. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.
Fardad Farahzad spoke in the Audio 24 episode about Trump's threat to deliver heavy blows to the Islamic Republic.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, November 2, 2026, that America's Arab allies in the Persian Gulf are preparing for possible extensive attacks by Washington on Iran. These attacks might begin this week and could be accompanied by retaliatory actions from the Islamic Republic against economic and civilian infrastructure in the region's countries. According to the newspaper, negotiations have not made significant progress despite efforts by the Donald Trump administration and Arab mediators.

Luis Enrique, head coach of Paris Saint-Germain, before the match against Villarreal in the UEFA Champions League, said that he was once considered an incompetent coach by many but now everyone thinks he is chosen, which he called a lie. He emphasized that coaches should not be judged based on short-term results and attributed his record of 127 wins to team cohesion, club support, and player quality. Enrique also warned that recent victories should not lead to over-optimism and that the team must play at its highest level.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International, saying about the low quality of bread in Iran: "The bread has become so low quality that it cannot be eaten. They neither taste good nor have a good color."

JD Vance, the US Vice President, announced on Monday, 11 Aban, that Washington has not set any deadline to reach an agreement with Iran before resuming military attacks. He said about the negotiation process with Tehran: "We have made progress and will see if we can make further progress."

It was reported that between 4 to 6 severe explosions and missile strikes occurred in Qeshm between 12:14 and 12:15. The explosion sounds were described as very loud and close. People in Qeshm were terrified by the intensity of the explosions and some felt shaking.

Trump stated that oil prices are falling at a dizzying speed, dropping nearly $10 per barrel. He said people feel that a war with Iran will not happen and that Iran wants to reach an agreement as soon as possible. Trump added that this might happen.

Raha Bahraini, a human rights lawyer and Amnesty International researcher on Iran, said the organization is launching a global campaign to gain support from UN General Assembly member states for establishing a special criminal justice mechanism. She added that war and regional tensions have diverted global attention from the killing of protesters in Dey 1404 and the increase in executions. Bahraini emphasized that documenting human rights violations is not enough, and without political will to establish an international court, the cycle of repression and impunity will continue.

Siamak Aram, a political analyst, said polls ahead of the US midterm elections indicate a better position for Democrats in the House of Representatives race, but the Senate election outcome remains uncertain. He added that Republicans still have a chance to maintain control of the Senate and the final result may differ from current estimates.

IRNA news agency reported five severe consecutive explosions on Monday evening on Qeshm Island and said some residents also observed two aircraft in the sky. The explosions occurred continuously and consecutively, and it seems the impact site was inside the island. Local and provincial sources have not yet made official statements about the cause of the explosions or the aircraft flights.

Iranian media reported that Hassan Habibi, former captain and coach of Iran's national football team, died at the age of 86 after several years of illness. Habibi was the first coach of Iran's national team after the Islamic Revolution and led the team to the 1980 Olympics. He also led the national team to third place in the 1980 Asian Cup in Kuwait.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that on the eve of the US congressional elections, no agreement has yet been reached between Washington and the Islamic Republic. He added that the US insists on stopping enrichment and handing over enriched uranium, while the Islamic Republic continues to oppose. Vaisi also noted that the possibility of a military attack remains and the opportunity for an agreement is diminishing each day.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, said the most likely scenario for the start of the war is a large-scale attack by heavy American bombers, including B-2, B-1, and B-52, on the Kalangazela facilities. This attack could quickly spread to missile cities, drone bases, military and governmental centers located in tunnels. It may also lead to the death of many officials and commanders of the Islamic Republic.

Ata Mohamad, an international relations expert, said that increased military pressure can bring the Islamic Republic closer to an agreement only if there is a way to end the conflict. He added that differences between the US and Israel regarding negotiations and continuing the war have led Tehran to emphasize maintaining its leverage. Mohamad also said that Gulf countries have not only strengthened their defense capabilities but also show signs of readiness for offensive actions.

The Saudi Arabian newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat reported that if the Democrats win the US House of Representatives elections, the political cost of escalating confrontation with Iran will increase for Donald Trump, the US president. Emirati media also warned that a potential escalation of tensions with the Islamic Republic could raise the price of oil to $120 per barrel.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, said that when he wore a Dumbledore costume for Halloween, he looked more like an Iranian sheikh than the US Vice President. He said he lost a bet with his children and had to wear the costume. Vance also complained about the Dumbledore wig, saying it was not comfortable to wear.

Sultan Al Jaber, CEO of Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, ADNOC, said that since the disruption in shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, nearly one billion barrels of oil reserves have been withdrawn. He warned that diesel reserves in some markets have reached their lowest seasonal level in 35 years and some markets face a shortage of 600 billion cubic feet of liquefied natural gas. Al Jaber emphasized that energy security depends not only on production levels but also on the secure transfer to markets, calling for increased strategic reserves and strengthened energy transfer routes.

According to media reports in Iran, a Qatari plane said to be carrying several officials from that country to Tehran has left Tehran. Previously, the Jamaran website reported that in continuation of regional diplomatic negotiations to reduce tensions, a delegation from Qatar headed by the senior advisor to the country's prime minister had arrived in Tehran.

Yahya Golmohammadi, head coach of Iran's U23 football team, stated in a TV interview regarding rumors of him replacing Amir Ghalenoei as national team coach that such questions are not good for the national team and Iranian football, and that Amir Ghalenoei is doing his job as head coach. He added that his goal is to have a good impact on young players and create an environment for them to help the national team, and he does not want to get involved in such matters. Golmohammadi also mentioned that they have not yet had a coordination meeting with Amir Ghalenoei, but they have had a good relationship previously.

Axios reported that Donald Trump is considering three options regarding Iran. JD Vance and Steve Witkoff favor a move toward an agreement and believe resuming war may not improve conditions. Benjamin Netanyahu and Pete Hegseth want to resume hostilities, while Scott Bassett, John Ratcliffe, and Marco Rubio recommend continuing economic pressure.
The Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, that the United States targeted Qeshm Island on Monday.

Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Turkey, in an interview with South Korea's Yonhap News Agency, emphasized the necessity of creating alternative and reliable routes for international trade due to the risks facing the global energy market and trade routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. He said Turkey is expanding transport connections between Asia and Europe and called on South Korean companies to invest more in the country's transport and logistics infrastructure projects.

Axios, quoting a US official, reported that the Revolutionary Guard fired a missile from Qeshm Island towards a US aircraft in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night. According to the official, a US fighter jet, in response, destroyed the Revolutionary Guard's surface-to-air missile launcher in a defensive action.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, said in an interview with Fox News that Iran is not in a suitable position for negotiations, but the likelihood of an agreement between Tehran and Washington is high. He referred to Iran's economic situation, saying its economy is collapsing due to sanctions and inflation is 301 percent. Trump also spoke about previous US attacks on Iran and his decision to start military operations, emphasizing that he will not allow Iran to have nuclear weapons.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, said that the continuation of the ceasefire could be a "double-edged sword" for the United States. He added that the Islamic Republic is using the opportunity amid economic pressure to rebuild its military capabilities. Satellite images indicate renewed activity at missile factories in Khajir, Parchin, and Shahroud, and ballistic missile production is underway again.

The competition between Republicans and Democrats for the U.S. Senate seat in Michigan involves two candidates with different backgrounds; Abdul Saeed, a Muslim doctor of Arab descent with Egyptian roots, is the Democratic candidate, facing Mike Rogers, a former Republican congressman.

The US midterm elections on 12 Aban 1405, corresponding to November 3, 2026, will not change the president, but the new composition of Congress could make it easier or harder to implement his policies towards Iran. Niloufar Mansouri, a reporter for Iran International, reports.

Shahram Kholdi, a Middle East history researcher, said military attacks alone are not enough to change Hezbollah's status, and the US and Israel now want to pressure the Lebanese government and army to disarm Hezbollah. He added that public dissatisfaction in Lebanon with Hezbollah's performance has created an opportunity for this goal. Kholdi emphasized that Israel has concluded that Lebanese society must also play a role in removing Hezbollah from the scene.

Several media outlets in Asia and Oceania have reported the possibility of a military attack by the US and Israel on the Islamic Republic. India Today has examined signs of preparation for a large-scale attack. South China Morning Post wrote about Netanyahu pressuring Trump to start attacks after the US elections.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in an interview with Israel's Channel 12 that he is not in a hurry to resume war with the Islamic Republic and prefers that economic pressures against Tehran continue for now. He emphasized that these pressures have paralyzed Iran's economy and that the Islamic Republic is more than ever since the start of the war seeking an agreement.

Fars News Agency reported that Hojjat Vafakardeh, a detective police officer in Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan province, was killed in an armed attack by unknown individuals. The Sistan and Baluchestan police information center stated that efforts by law enforcement and security forces to identify and arrest the perpetrators of this attack continue.

Kayhan newspaper wrote that the interests and facilities of the US and NATO in Europe, including in the UK, Italy, Greece, Romania, and Cyprus, could be targeted by the Islamic Republic's missiles if another war occurs. The newspaper referred to Mojtaba Khamenei's order for a military response "without geographical limitation" and added that the range of potential targets could extend to the "heart of Europe." Kayhan also wrote that the Islamic Republic's missiles have the capability to target NATO bases at distances of four to five thousand kilometers.

The Hamshahri newspaper reported on November 3 that the target list of the Islamic Republic's armed forces is updated without geographical limits. It was reported that if the US and Israel attack Iran's strategic infrastructure, the conflict could expand to American bases in Europe. The newspaper also mentioned that with the increased range of ballistic missiles, US bases in Europe could be potential targets in a new war.

The Asian Football Confederation announced that the 2027 AFC Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been postponed due to attacks by Houthi forces supported by the Islamic Republic. The tournament with 24 teams will be held from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028. The organizing committee stated the schedule changed due to exceptional conditions and extensive logistical complexities.

Mizan News Agency reported the execution of Amirhossein Maleki and Amirhossein Ebrahimi, two protesters arrested during the January 2026 protests, in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan. Hassan Qashqavi, spokesperson for the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that in case of a military attack on the Islamic Republic, the geographical scope of the possible war could be on the scale of World War III. The order to cut internet in Iran usually comes from the Supreme National Security Council, but the key to the cut is pressed by a network of 690 managers and 298 companies, including the Execution of Imam Khomeini's Order and the Revolutionary Guards. This network controls and intermittently cuts the communications of the Iranian people. Companies that describe themselves as "private" and "knowledge-based" are also active in providing hardware and software for monitoring and filtering.

A number of street cleaners in Tehran held a protest in front of the city's municipality building. The cleaners demanded the fulfillment of officials' promises regarding direct employment with the municipality and clarification of their job status.
